The Backlog Is Not the Quarter

mentions.excerpt: Steve Eisman, in a conversation with Ed Zitron, draws the darker inference: data centers are harder and costlier to build than planned, gigawatt projects are late, and every month of slippage gives customers who already lose money more time to stumble.

Ed Zitron said Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Microsoft have together spent over $1 trillion on Nvidia GPUs, mostly to win the business of OpenAI and Anthropic, two companies they also help fund and that both lose heavily.
Against that growth sits the loss-making base of the chain: Steve Eisman, in an episode with Ed Zitron, cited OpenAI’s $20.9 billion loss in 2025 on $13.07 billion of revenue.

mentions.section: The margin the book does not show
mentions.excerpt: Eisman, in a September 9 episode with Ed Zitron, notes that Nvidia stretched payment terms for investment-grade customers to a full year from 90 days, adding 14 days to days sales outstanding, and on September 14 adds that five customers made up 70% of Nvidia's accounts receivable, some of them, OpenAI among them, not in especially healthy condition.

Ed Zitron, Steve Eisman's guest on The Real Eisman Playbook on September 9, said Nvidia had extended payment terms for investment-grade customers from 90 days to a full year and tied that to 14 more days outstanding.

sides.question: cash-or-loop
sides.claim: Over $1T of GPUs bought to win two unprofitable labs, the source of about 70% of hyperscaler AI revenue.
